title: The Lantern Man of the Fens

scenes.narration: The light was moving against the wind, low over the black water, and the old men told the boy never to whistle at it.
In the fen villages of eastern England, people called it the Lantern Man, a glowing shape that drifted over the marsh at night.
The story goes that a farmhand named Tom walked home late across the dyke path and saw the lantern swinging ahead of him.
He laughed and whistled to it, the way the old men warned against, and the light stopped, then turned toward him.
It came faster than a man could run, skimming the reeds, and Tom threw himself face down into the mud as the villagers advised.
The people believed the Lantern Man would pass over anyone lying flat, and in the tale the light swept past him and was gone.
Tom never whistled on the fen again, and for years he told anyone who would listen that the light had been looking for him.
Some say it was marsh gas. The fen villages still say: if you see the lantern, keep your mouth shut and lie down.
